entries.en: RESERVE[n]Mythology

The greatest angel[n]in Judeo-Christian[n]legend. He is known[n]as the Voice of God[n]or the Angel of[n]Contracts. Despite[n]his duty to maintain[n]the world's order,[n]he shows no mercy[n]towards humanity.
Demonic Lord of the[n]Flies whose insect[n]minions carry souls[n]for him to control.[n]He is mentioned in the[n]Bible as a leader of[n]evil spirits and is seen[n]as a powerful demon.

A hero in Celtic[n]folklore. He was[n]called Setanta until[n]he earned the name,[n]"Culann's Hound."[n]There are many tales[n]of his adventures.[n]He received his spear,[n]Gae Bolg, from his[n]mentor, Scathach.
A drunkard who[n]tricked the Devil[n]out of taking him to[n]Hell. When refused[n]entry to Heaven, he[n]was forced to wander[n]the earth with only[n]an ember as a light.
A winter fairy of[n]European descent.[n]He leaves ice[n]patterns on windows[n]and nips people's[n]noses. Though[n]normally an innocent[n]creature, he will[n]freeze his victims to[n]death if provoked.
Friendly fairies of[n]the forest that[n]tend to hide from[n]humans. They like[n]to play tricks on[n]the Laz people. It[n]is said they are[n]the souls of dead,[n]unbaptized children.
The guardian hound[n]who prevents[n]anyone from[n]entering or exiting[n]the underworld in[n]Greek lore. It was[n]born from Typhon[n]and Echidna, and is[n]the older brother of[n]Orthrus.
A demon who tempts[n]sleeping men and[n]attacks infants.[n]She is the daughter[n]of the demoness,[n]Lilith. Like her[n]mother, she drains[n]men of their essence.
One of the 72[n]demons of the[n]Goetia. He looks[n]like a knight and[n]has the power to[n]see things to come.[n]He also knows[n]much about war.
The father of all[n]gods in Norse[n]legend. He willingly[n]sacrificed one eye[n]to gain wisdom. In[n]preparation for[n]Ragnarok, he gathers[n]the souls of fallen[n]warriors to his hall,[n]Valhalla.

A spirit of Chinese[n]folklore who dwells[n]in trees once used[n]for hangings. She is[n]smaller than a human[n]and cannot speak,[n]but her voice is said[n]to be as clear and[n]as beautiful as[n]a bird's song.
One of the 72[n]demons of the[n]Goetia, this demon[n]appears as a[n]pentacle. Keeper[n]of jewels and herbal[n]lore, Decarabia is[n]said to have the[n]ability to shape-[n]shift at will.
A Buddhist demon[n]that represents the[n]fear of death. Also[n]known as "The Evil[n]One," he sent his[n]daughters to tempt[n]Buddha during his[n]meditations.
One of the 72[n]demons of the[n]Goetia, he is known[n]as the President of[n]Hell. He can shape-[n]shift from leopard to[n]human and reveal[n]the truth behind[n]divine mysteries.

The Norse thunder[n]god and son of Odin,[n]Thor owns the power[n]enhancing belt,[n]Megingjard, and[n]wields Mjolnir, a[n]hammer that causes[n]lightning to strike[n]and returns to its[n]owner if thrown.
A legendary white[n]horse with a single[n]spiral horn. It can[n]only be tamed by a[n]pure maiden, and its[n]horn supposedly has[n]miraculous healing[n]capabilities.
One of the four[n]major archangels.[n]His name means[n]"Flame of God,"[n]and he knows all[n]the celestial[n]phenomena. He is[n]the first angel[n]Satan met on earth.
The Hindu goddess[n]of rivers, and[n]patron of speech,[n]writing, learning,[n]the arts, and[n]sciences. Brahma[n]is her husband.
"Choosers of the[n]slain" in Norse[n]lore. Armed with[n]shining armor and[n]swords, they look[n]for brave warriors[n]to take to Valhalla,[n]so that they may[n]fight in Ragnarok.

A female demon in[n]Hindu lore. Though[n]originally a Dravidian[n]fertility goddess, the[n]spread of Hinduism[n]changed perception[n]of her to a demonic[n]figure. Usually[n]depicted as a nude,[n]voluptuous, female.

The Hindu elephant-[n]headed god. He was[n]originally created by[n]Parvati in order to[n]prevent anyone from[n]watching her bathe.[n]Shiva batted off his[n]original head and[n]replaced it with an[n]elephant's head.
The jackal-headed[n]god of the dead and[n]embalming from[n]Egyptian myth. He[n]weighs the hearts[n]of the dead to[n]determine their[n]final destination.
The Canaanite god[n]of death. Every[n]year he attempts[n]to kill Baal, the[n]god of fertility,[n]only to see him[n]raised from the[n]dead with the help[n]of Baal's sister,[n]Anat.
One of the four[n]major archangels,[n]his name means[n]"healer." He recites[n]the history of the[n]fallen angels and[n]the creation of[n]Adam and Eve.
A warrior woman[n]of the Land of[n]Shadows in Celtic[n]lore. She taught the[n]hero, Cu Chulainn,[n]the art of war and[n]gave him the spear,[n]Gae Bolg.
The leader of a[n]swarm of pixies.[n]Any pixie in a[n]leadership role[n]or with remarkable[n]power is called by[n]this name.
A mystical creature[n]in Balinese lore,[n]it represents good[n]and is Rangda's[n]eternal rival.[n]Even if defeated,[n]it will be reborn.[n]The result is a[n]never-ending[n]struggle...
A giant elephant[n]monster of Sri[n]Lankan myth, it is[n]typically portrayed[n]as being ridden by[n]the Evil One, Mara.[n]Whoever looks into[n]its evil eye is said[n]to be met with[n]misfortune.
The king of snow[n]who rules over an[n]infinite number of[n]Jack Frosts. He has[n]the power to freeze[n]the entire world,[n]but is unaware of[n]it due to his naïve[n]personality.
A young man of[n]Greek myth. He[n]rejected the nymph[n]Echo, who faded to[n]a whisper out of[n]despair. Cursed by[n]Nemesis, he fell[n]in love with his[n]own reflection and[n]wasted away.

Osiris's wife as[n]well as his younger[n]sister. Upon the[n]death of her husband,[n]she revived him with[n]her incredible magic[n]power. Isis is seen[n]at many gravesites[n]as the guardian[n]goddess of the dead.
A serpentine[n]woman of Greek[n]myth, she was once[n]the queen of Libya.[n]Zeus's jealous wife,[n]Hera, killed her[n]children, causing[n]her to go mad and[n]transform into[n]a monster.
The spirit who[n]said, "For we are[n]many," in ancient[n]scriptures. The[n]name comes from[n]the Roman military[n]term for an army[n]unit of 3,000 to[n]6,000 men.

A Hindu demon. He[n]is an enemy of the[n]gods and attacks[n]humans to feed off[n]of them. His hideous[n]appearance strikes[n]fear into those who[n]see him. Rakshasa[n]shape-shifts to[n]deceive his enemies.
Evil spirits of[n]Murngin lore[n]believed to be[n]reborn shadows.[n]They kidnap and[n]eat children, and[n]strike down any[n]sorcerer who uses[n]black magic.
One of the 72[n]demons of the[n]Goetia, he appears[n]as a great sea[n]monster. Known as[n]the great Marquis of[n]Hell, he is skilled[n]linguistically, and is[n]a master of rhetoric.
A brave young man[n]in Celtic myth.[n]After defeating a[n]fierce guard dog, he[n]volunteered to take[n]its place, earning[n]him the nickname[n]"Hound of Culann."
The queen of the[n]fairies and Oberon's[n]wife. She is derived[n]from the Roman[n]goddess Diana.[n]She was later[n]immortalized in[n]Shakespeare's play[n]"A Midsummer Night's[n]Dream."
A male demon of[n]European lore in[n]medieval times.[n]They visit sleeping[n]women and have[n]sexual intercourse[n]with them. The[n]resulting children[n]become witches[n]or wizards.
An evil monster[n]from Japanese lore[n]known for its[n]hideous appearance[n]and brute strength.[n]They loot and plunder[n]villages, massacring[n]the townspeople with[n]their iron clubs.

Said to have been[n]Adam's first wife,[n]she desired to be[n]his equal and[n]refused to obey him.[n]She was cast out of[n]Eden and became a[n]demon of the night.[n]She is the mother of[n]the demoness, Lilim.
A wicked witch of[n]Balinese lore, she[n]represents evil[n]and is Barong's[n]eternal rival.[n]Even if defeated,[n]she will come back[n]to life, and their[n]battle will have[n]no end.
A divine wolf god[n]in Japanese folklore,[n]also written as[n]"Oguchi-no-Magami."[n]It is often drawn on[n]prayer boards to[n]prevent fires and[n]thefts, but it is[n]also feared as a[n]human-eater.
A beautiful Hindu[n]goddess of love and[n]one of Shiva's wives.[n]Always by his side,[n]she played a role in[n]opening his third[n]eye. She can turn[n]into Durga or Kali[n]when angered.

One of the four[n]major archangels.[n]She is also the only[n]female angel at this[n]rank. Her name comes[n]from the Sumerian[n]word for "governor."[n]She is the angel who[n]told Mary of her[n]pregnancy.
Repeller of evil[n]found at Kinpusen[n]by En-no-Ozunu.[n]Believed to be a[n]fusion of Buddha,[n]Guanyin, and[n]Maitreya, he is a god[n]who originated from[n]Japan rather than[n]the Buddhavacana.

A mysterious blonde[n]girl. She is quite[n]powerful, despite[n]her looks. Some say[n]she is the ghost of[n]a girl who died a[n]sad death. Others[n]say she is a spirit[n]born from someone's[n]imagination.

A goddess of death[n]and destruction. She[n]is said to be another[n]face of Parvati. She[n]is violent, wears a[n]string of skulls,[n]and carries bloody[n]weapons, but she[n]also blesses her[n]followers.
A type of tengu said[n]to have lived on Mt.[n]Kurama in Kyoto. The[n]most powerful and[n]well-known of the[n]tengu, they have the[n]power to fend off[n]disease and bring[n]good fortune.

The king of the[n]fairies and Titania's[n]husband. He is quite[n]old, but due to a[n]curse, his looks are[n]that of a young boy.[n]He often flirts with[n]human women, ending[n]in a scolding from[n]his wife.

An exceptionally[n]powerful shikigami.[n]Only the most elite[n]onmyoji are able to[n]summon and bind it[n]to paper. It can ward[n]off disaster or cure[n]illness, but its[n]ordinary temperament[n]is quite vicious.

A giant snake with[n]eight heads that[n]Susano-o defeated to[n]save Kushinada-Hime.[n]The legendary sword[n]Ame-no-Murakumo-no-[n]Tsurugi, also known[n]as the "Sword of[n]Kusanagi," emerged[n]from its belly.
One of the 72 demons[n]of the Goetia. Known[n]as the Prince of Hell,[n]he appears as a horse[n]and answers questions[n]of the past, present,[n]and future. He is faithful[n]to his conjurer.

A monkey god of[n]Hindu descent. His[n]father is Vayu, the[n]wind god. Extremely[n]nimble, he performed[n]many heroic deeds in[n]the Ramayana. He is[n]powerful, can fly, and[n]can change his shape[n]into many forms.

Eighth of the nine[n]orders of angels.[n]Their duty is to[n]minister to humans[n]and deliver messages.[n]They are warriors of[n]Heaven and lead[n]Heaven's forces[n]during battle with[n]the armies of evil.

A "piggyback[n]monster" of Japan[n]that jumps on the[n]backs of those who[n]pass grassy paths.[n]It is heavy and not[n]easily removed, but[n]will turn into gold[n]coins if you can[n]carry it back home.
The fairy queen in[n]Celtic myth. Often[n]identified with[n]Titania. She would[n]offer mead mixed[n]with her blood to[n]her many consorts.
Metatron's twin[n]brother in Judeo-[n]Christian lore, he[n]is the master of[n]heavenly songs.[n]It is said that a[n]human would take[n]500 years to walk[n]the length of his[n]body.
The "Destroyer"[n]and "Angel of the[n]Bottomless Pit,"[n]as described in[n]ancient scriptures.[n]He controls locusts[n]and uses them to[n]cause massive[n]destruction to[n]villages.

A holy beast said[n]to protect houses[n]from evil and bring[n]good fortune. They[n]look similar to Shinto[n]guardian dogs, but[n]are actually modeled[n]after a lion. There[n]are many stories about[n]it in Ryukyu lore.
A fairy in German[n]folklore who carries[n]a bag of magical[n]sand, which puts[n]humans to sleep[n]when thrown into[n]their eyes. If the[n]victim resists, the[n]Sandman will sit[n]on their eyelids.
One of the 72[n]demons of the[n]Goetia. He led[n]Sodom and[n]Gomorrah to ruin[n]and persecuted[n]Jesus. He grants[n]high social status[n]to those who[n]summon him.
A beautiful fairy[n]of Irish lore that[n]yearns for the love[n]of a human man. She[n]drains the life of[n]her lovers in return[n]for granting them[n]artistic inspiration.

The Phrygian mother[n]goddess of the earth,[n]she is often depicted[n]with wild animals, and[n]lions in particular.[n]She had her priest,[n]Attis, as a lover, but[n]drove him insane when[n]he was forced to[n]marry another.

A cursed god of[n]death, evil, and the[n]night in Slavic lore.[n]His name means[n]"Black God," and he[n]is the counterpart[n]of the "White God,"[n]Belobog. Despite[n]being feared, he was[n]also worshipped.
One of the 72 demons[n]of the Goetia. He[n]appears as a leopard[n]and can see the past[n]and future. He can[n]control fire and burn[n]all his adversaries[n]to death.
A one-eyed, one-[n]legged monster[n]said to live deep in[n]the mountains of[n]Kumano, Japan. It's[n]believed to be the[n]degraded blacksmith[n]god, Ame no Me-[n]Hitotsu no Kami.
The two-headed pet[n]dog belonging to[n]the giant, Geryon,[n]in Greek myth. He[n]guarded a herd of[n]red oxen, but was[n]killed by Hercules[n]during one of his[n]twelve labors.
A female demon of[n]European lore in[n]medieval times.[n]They visit sleeping[n]men and have sexual[n]intercourse with[n]them. The victims[n]don't wake up but[n]may dream of the[n]encounter.

A cryptid sighted[n]during the 60s-80s[n]in West Virginia. It[n]has shining red eyes[n]and is named for the[n]fin-like appendages[n]on its sides. It uses its[n]keen sense for blood[n]to track down the[n]source and feed on it.
Taira no Masakado,[n]hero of the Heian[n]period. He claimed[n]the title "Shinno"[n](New Emperor) and[n]rebelled against[n]the government. He[n]was killed, but it[n]is said he became[n]a demigod.
The fourth of the[n]nine orders of[n]angels. Their duty[n]is to oversee the[n]other angels. Their[n]actions are the[n]manifestation of[n]God's will.
Long-lived cats[n]are said to become[n]these malevolent[n]cat demons. Their[n]powers vary[n]according to how[n]long they have[n]lived, ranging from[n]shape-shifting to[n]controlling the dead.
A Jack Frost that[n]yearned for evil.[n]This powerful demon[n]is born when a[n]cute Jack Frost[n]remembers its[n]nature as a demon.

A mysterious god of[n]ancient Japan. Most[n]famously worshipped[n]by Nagasunehiko, who[n]was defeated in battle[n]against Emperor Jinmu,[n]Arahabaki came to be[n]treated as a symbol of[n]rebellion and defiance.
Ninth of the nine[n]orders of angels.[n]They are closest in[n]nature to humans.[n]They watch over[n]individuals and warn[n]those who stray[n]from the path.
A Norse giantess[n]called the "snow-[n]shoe goddess" and[n]the embodiment of[n]winter. According to[n]legend, all the gods[n]will return to her at[n]the end of Ragnarok.
The goddess of life[n]in Shinto myth. She[n]once mediated[n]between Izanagi[n]and Izanami during[n]their confrontation[n]in Yomi, the land[n]of the dead.
A Chinese god of[n]war, he is said to[n]have invented many[n]weapons. He and[n]his followers[n]rebelled against[n]the Yellow Emperor,[n]Huang Di, but were[n]ultimately defeated.
The sixth of the[n]nine orders of[n]angels. It is said[n]that they were the[n]first order to be[n]created. Their[n]duty is to protect[n]human souls from[n]demons.
A dog spirit said to[n]possess people in[n]Japanese lore.[n]Those possessed[n]are in a state of[n]"inu-tsuki" and[n]lose consciousness.[n]Onmyoji use Inugami[n]as familiars.
The general of Hell.[n]He keeps watch over[n]other demons. One[n]of Hell's greatest[n]necromancers, he[n]can control souls[n]and corpses.
Among the eight[n]Yashaou and one[n]of Bishamonten's[n]attendants.[n]Originally a child-[n]eating demon, he[n]was converted by theBuddha and becamea protector figure.
A primitive monster[n]with a viscous body.[n]There are various[n]theories as to its[n]origin, but it is[n]still under debate.[n]Said to compulsively[n]collect shiny objects.
An evil deity of[n]Mesopotamian[n]folklore with[n]an eagle's body[n]and lion's head.[n]While the god Enlil[n]purified himself,[n]Anzu stole the[n]Tablets of Destiny[n]from him.
A divine creature in[n]Japanese lore. They[n]are three-legged[n]birds sent by[n]Amaterasu to help[n]humans. They are[n]said to have helped[n]Emperor Jinmu claim[n]victory.
A Japanese general[n]of the Genpei War[n]near the end of the[n]Heian era and start of[n]the Kamakura era. His[n]bold ingenuity and[n]ruthless skill with a[n]blade are still praised[n]in Japan today.
A Japanese god of[n]war, hunting, and[n]fertility. He fought[n]Take-Mikazuchi for[n]control of Japan and[n]lost. He escaped[n]to Suwa, but was[n]prohibited to leave[n]since.
Japanese goddess[n]of entertainment,[n]she governs many[n]sacred dances. She[n]is most famous for[n]luring out Amaterasu,[n]who had barricaded[n]herself inside a cave.
A Japanese goddess.[n]She governs fields[n]and fertility. All[n]of her sisters were[n]sacrificed to[n]Yamata-no-Orochi,[n]but she was saved[n]by Susano-o and[n]became his wife.

A Buddhist demon[n]said to drain human[n]life energy. He has[n]dark skin, stands 3[n]meters tall, and[n]sometimes changes[n]his shape to a gourd.[n]Known to have once[n]served Rudra, the[n]god of storms.
One of the four[n]oni controlled by[n]Fujiwara no Chikata.[n]By eliminating its[n]aura and preventing[n]others from sensing[n]its presence, it is[n]able to surprise its[n]enemies.

One of the four oni[n]controlled by[n]Fujiwara no Chikata,[n]its body is so hard[n]that no weapons[n]can penetrate it.[n]It and its comrades[n]fell into hell through[n]holes that can still be[n]found in modern Iga.
One of the four[n]oni controlled by[n]Fujiwara no Chikata,[n]it can cause floods[n]with the swing of its[n]arms. In the Taiheiki,[n]Ki no Tomoo expelled[n]the oni by reading a[n]Japanese poem.
One of the four oni[n]controlled by[n]Fujiwara no Chikata,[n]it sends hurricanes[n]to blow away its[n]enemies. Some say[n]that Fuu-ki is the[n]original ninja.
The Hindu king[n]of birds. In the[n]Ramayana, he[n]fought bravely[n]against Ravana[n]in an attempt to[n]save Sita, Rama's[n]wife and the 7th[n]avatar of Vishnu,[n]but lost.
A god in Assyrian[n]legend, his name[n]is interchangeable[n]with Sakkut,[n]another incarnation[n]of the star-god,[n]Saturn.
A horse-like fairy[n]of Celtic folklore[n]that lives by the[n]water. It drowns[n]those who ride on[n]it, but is a valuable[n]mount if you can[n]tame it.
Egyptian moon god[n]that takes the[n]form of a baboon,[n]he is the one who[n]measures time. He[n]gave Isis the power[n]to resurrect Osiris[n]after he was killed[n]by the evil god Seth.
The Greek god of[n]wine and theater. He[n]was originally a god[n]of life protecting[n]the mountains of[n]Thrace. He taught[n]humans how to make[n]wine.
Hindu water spirits,[n]they are beautiful[n]young women who[n]dance for the gods.[n]They also guide[n]heroes fallen in[n]battle to paradise.

One of the 72[n]demons of the[n]Goetia. The great[n]Marquis of Hell, he[n]appears where there[n]is battle to stoke the[n]hatred within soldiers.[n]He helps defeat the[n]enemies of those[n]who summon him.
BLANK
Small human-like[n]creatures, that[n]have kind, calm[n]personalities. Once[n]coexisting with the[n]Ainu people of Japan,[n]there was a falling[n]out at some point,[n]and they disappeared.
A type of tengu.[n]Their spiritual[n]power is weaker than[n]other tengu, so they[n]are much smaller.[n]They are said to be[n]the reincarnations[n]of long-lived wolves.

A bluish-tinged[n]diamond that[n]Napoléon Bonaparte[n]had mounted to the[n]pommel of his sword.[n]It was named after[n]the French Regent[n]Philippe II, Duke of[n]Orléans, who had[n]purchased it in 1717.
The diamond[n]necklace that[n]Jeanne de la Motte[n]swindled from[n]jewelers in 1785 by[n]claiming it was on[n]behalf of the Queen[n]of France, Marie[n]Antoinette.
Also known as the[n]Stone of Destiny,[n]it is a stone used[n]in the coronations[n]of Scotland's[n]monarchs. Legends[n]say the stone is[n]linked to angels.

Once called the[n]world's largest[n]diamond, it was cut[n]when it came to[n]the British royal[n]family. It is said to[n]bring bad luck to any[n]man who wears it,[n]so only the females[n]have ever adorned it.
A diamond stolen[n]from a Hindu[n]temple that is[n]said to drive its[n]owner to their[n]death. It was cut[n]into smaller pieces[n]in an attempt to[n]break the curse.
Also known as[n]Charlemagne's[n]talisman, it is said[n]to make its owner an[n]emperor. In between[n]the two gems is a[n]piece of Jesus'[n]cross and a hair of[n]the Virgin Mary.

Unlike its name[n]suggests, the Hope[n]Diamond is a cursed[n]jewel that brings[n]ruin from one owner[n]to the next. A few[n]supposed victims[n]include King Louis[n]XVI and his wife,[n]Marie Antoinette.
An ancient Out-Of-[n]Place-Artifact found[n]in Central and[n]South America. It is[n]said that if you[n]collect 13 of them in[n]one spot, the truth[n]of the universe[n]will be revealed.
A metal mentioned[n]in ancient Greek[n]literature. Some[n]accounts say it was[n]merely brass, but[n]other stories suggest[n]it was, in fact, a[n]legendary material.

A magical plant[n]whose roots look[n]like a human. They[n]are valued for their[n]healing properties[n]in potions, but the[n]screams they let out[n]when pulled from the[n]ground will kill[n]anyone who hears them.
The chief Semitic[n]god who governs[n]over fertility. He is[n]the god of Canaan[n]and brother and[n]consort to the[n]goddess Anat, who[n]saved him from Mot.
Hindu deities[n]of passion and[n]relations. They are[n]Kali's attendants.[n]They eat human[n]flesh and gather[n]at graveyards and[n]crematories each[n]night. Their name[n]means "sky dancer."
A fairy of England[n]and Scotland.[n]She carries out[n]household chores[n]while everyone[n]sleeps and is a[n]welcome spirit. It[n]is said you can hear[n]her silk skirt rustle[n]as she works.
A Welsh creature[n]commonly known as[n]"Bugbear" or the[n]"Boogeyman." Its[n]existence is often[n]used by mothers to[n]scare children into[n]behaving.
A mass of malevolent[n]intent and emotion[n]that failed to become[n]a true demon. All it[n]does is eat prey[n]and grow.

An evil creature[n]with two curving[n]horns. It represents[n]impurity, unlike[n]the Unicorn. Said[n]to be derived from[n]Re'em in the Bible.[n]Another legend says[n]that it feeds off of[n]disloyal husbands.
